notes: PCI Express 5.0 does not specify OTP / fuse content as a protocol concept. Vendor ID / Device ID / Revision ID / Class Code are burned so Configuration Reads return correct identifiers after PERST# deassertion. For Gen5, the supported-link-speeds advertisement (with the 32.0 GT/s bit) and per-lane equalization preset capabilities are hardware-determined; default EQ presets and Lane Margining capabilities may be factory-fixed in the PHY.

device_identification_register_content.access: Read-only via IDCODE instruction; parallel-loaded with the hard-wired value in CaptureDR; shifted out on TDO in ShiftDR.

usercode_register_content.access: Read-only via USERCODE instruction; shares the Device Identification register but loads a user-programmed value (e.g. FPGA bitstream version, customer revision).
usercode_register_content.writability: Vendor-defined; in CPLD / FPGA parts the USERCODE register is loaded at configuration time from the bitstream, so it is functionally programmable (not strictly OTP) for those devices.

otp_equivalent_factory_burned_fields.note: Assigned by PCI-SIG to the silicon vendor.
Per-product identifier chosen by the vendor.
Base Class + Sub-Class + Programming Interface; identifies the device category.
Per-board subsystem identification (typically the integrator's IDs).
Some templates may be silicon-fixed; address/data values themselves are programmed at runtime.

otp_equivalent_factory_burned_fields.field: Supported Link Speeds Vector (incl. 32.0 GT/s bit)
otp_equivalent_factory_burned_fields.note: Hardware-fixed advertisement of supported rates; a Gen5 device sets the 32.0 GT/s bit.
